learning: If line_loss_events on the s-bend and slalom falls to 0 with max_error below 0.06 m, keep the span and stop changing body parameters. If one line loss per run persists at the floor, the span is not enough, so test a wider span toward ±0.08 m. If the oval finish rate falls and steering_oscillation rises above about 0.3, the wider bar is adding overshoot, so reduce kd before changing geometry.
notes: Iteration 9 platform with the sensor span widened to ±0.06 m at 30 mm pitch, controller unchanged from iteration 9 so the span effect is isolated.
rationale: The Builder's iteration 10 geometry widens the sensor span to ±0.06 m at 30 mm pitch, keeping the iteration 9 platform otherwise fixed. Iteration 9 showed that the controller change (base_speed 1.0, kp 2.5, kd 0.4) cleared the oval line loss, with 19 of 20 finishes at 0.1 line-loss events, but the s-bend and slalom still ended off_track with one line loss per run and max_error at the 0.062 to 0.063 m floor. Those are the tracks where the line leaves the old ±0.04 m span, so the wider span is the untested lever for them. Five sensors at these x positions still span the tape across the wider range, so I keep sensor_weights at [-2,-1,0,1,2]. Because the reading-weighted average is bounded by the largest weight, this keeps the signal scale in the range the controller was tuned for, and the same weight pattern is the Builder's own suggestion. I leave the controller gains unchanged (base_speed 1.0, kp 2.5, ki 0.05, kd 0.4, last_direction) so that any change in s-bend or slalom line losses is attributable to span. I expect line_loss_events on the s-bend and slalom to fall toward 0 and max_error to drop below about 0.06 m, with the oval finish rate held near 95 percent. I make no claim about the result, since nothing has raced for this design.
